title: Scheduling, Resources and Autoscaling

header.html: Configure Pod admission and scheduling (limits, node affinity, etc.); Configure workload autoscaling

toc.title: Pod admission controls: LimitRange and ResourceQuota

html:
1How scheduling works

The scheduler takes each Pod without a node and picks one in two steps: filter (which nodes can run it: enough free resources, matching selectors, taints tolerated) and score (which of those is best). If the filter step leaves no node, the Pod stays Pending and kubectl describe pod shows a FailedScheduling event that says why (for example "Insufficient cpu", "node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector", "node(s) had untolerated taint"). That event is the first thing to read for any Pending Pod.

2Requests, limits and QoS

Field Meaning
resources.requests what the scheduler reserves for the container; used to choose a node
resources.limits the ceiling at run time; CPU over the limit is throttled, memory over the limit is OOM-killed 
k set resources deployment app --requests=cpu=100m,memory=64Mi --limits=cpu=200m,memory=128Mi   # workloads with a Pod template
k run sized --image=nginx:alpine --dry-run=client -o yaml > pod.yaml                                # a bare Pod: generate YAML, add the resources block, apply

kubectl run has no --requests/--limits flags in the kubectl used here (v1.36; kubectl run --help lists only --env, --overrides, --port among the setting flags), so a Pod with resources is written in YAML (or created from --dry-run=client -o yaml output). CPU is in cores (1 = one core, 100m = 0.1 core). Memory is in bytes (64Mi, 1Gi). A request larger than any node can offer (for example cpu: "100") keeps the Pod Pending forever (Lab 6.8).

QoS class (shown in .status.qosClass) decides who is evicted first under memory pressure:

Class Rule
Guaranteed every container has requests = limits for CPU and memory
Burstable at least one request or limit set, not Guaranteed
BestEffort no requests or limits at all (evicted first)

3Pod admission controls: LimitRange and ResourceQuota

Both are checked when an object is created (admission), per namespace.

LimitRange sets defaults and min/max per container or Pod:

apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata: {name: defaults}
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Container
    defaultRequest: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}   # applied when a container has no request
    default: {cpu: 250m, memory: 128Mi}         # applied when a container has no limit
    # max / min / maxLimitRequestRatio also exist

The defaults are written into the Pod at creation, so k get pod -o yaml shows them. Existing Pods are not changed.

ResourceQuota caps the total for a namespace:

k -n quota create quota team-quota --hard=pods=3,requests.cpu=1,requests.memory=1Gi
k -n quota describe quota team-quota        # Used vs Hard
  • If a quota covers CPU or memory, every new Pod must declare that resource (or a LimitRange must supply a default), otherwise it is rejected.
  • A Deployment over quota does not fail loudly: the ReplicaSet cannot create the extra Pods. Read k -n quota describe rs or k -n quota get events for "exceeded quota" (Lab 6.3).

4Choosing nodes

Tool Use
nodeSelector simplest: Pod runs only on nodes with these labels
nodeName bypass the scheduler (rarely used)
Node affinity richer rules: In, NotIn, Exists; required or preferred
Pod affinity / anti-affinity place Pods near or away from other Pods
Taints and tolerations nodes repel Pods unless they tolerate
Topology spread constraints spread Pods evenly across zones or nodes 
k label node cka-worker2 disk=ssd           # add a label
k label node cka-worker2 disk-              # remove it
k get nodes --show-labels

Node affinity (required):

spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
          - {key: tier, operator: In, values: [gold]}
  • required... is a hard rule: no match, Pod stays Pending. preferred... (with a weight) is a soft rule.
  • ...IgnoredDuringExecution means Pods already running are not moved if labels change later.

Pod anti-affinity (spread replicas across nodes):

spec:
  affinity:
    podAntiAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - labelSelector: {matchLabels: {app: ha-web}}
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname

Topology spread constraints (topologySpreadConstraints with maxSkew, topologyKey, whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule|ScheduleAnyway, labelSelector) spread replicas evenly. Trap found in the lab: the tainted control plane node still counts as an empty domain, so with DoNotSchedule only 2 of 4 replicas schedule on a 2-worker cluster until you add nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor (Lab 6.10).

With required and only N usable nodes, replica N+1 stays Pending. In the lab cluster the control plane is tainted, so two workers allow two replicas (Lab 6.7).

5Taints and tolerations

A taint on a node says "keep Pods away unless they tolerate me". Format key=value:effect.

Effect Behavior
NoSchedule new Pods are not scheduled unless they tolerate it
PreferNoSchedule the scheduler avoids the node if it can
NoExecute also evicts running Pods that do not tolerate it 
k taint node cka-worker2 dedicated=db:NoSchedule
k taint node cka-worker2 dedicated-                 # remove the taint (note the trailing -)

tolerations:
- {key: dedicated, operator: Equal, value: db, effect: NoSchedule}
- {key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, operator: Exists, effect: NoSchedule}

A toleration only allows a Pod onto the node; it does not attract it. To force a Pod onto a tainted node, combine the toleration with a nodeSelector or node affinity (Lab 6.6). The control plane node carries the taint node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule, which is why DaemonSets need the toleration to reach it.

6Workload autoscaling

The HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) changes a workload's replica count from observed metrics.

k autoscale deployment web --min=2 --max=5 --cpu=50%
k get hpa
k describe hpa web
  • It needs the Metrics Server (the source for kubectl top) and the Pods must declare a CPU request: utilization is a percentage of the request. Without a request the HPA shows <unknown> and does not scale.
  • Formula in words: desired replicas = current replicas x (current utilization / target utilization), rounded up, kept between min and max.
  • autoscaling/v2 also supports memory and custom metrics, and a behavior section for scale-up and scale-down speed.
  • Vertical Pod Autoscaling (changing requests) is a separate add-on and is not part of the core exam objectives.

7Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m06 -->

Lab 6.1: requests limits

Domain: Workloads | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-01-requests-limits)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace res, create a Pod sized (image nginx:alpine) with CPU request 100m, memory request 64Mi, CPU limit 200m and memory limit 128Mi.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n res run sized --image=nginx:alpine --dry-run=client -o yaml > /tmp/sized.yaml
sed -i 's/^  containers:/  containers:/; s/^    resources: {}/    resources: {requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}, limits: {cpu: 200m, memory: 128Mi}}/' /tmp/sized.yaml
kubectl -n res apply -f /tmp/sized.yaml
kubectl -n res wait --for=condition=Ready pod/sized --timeout=120s
kubectl -n res get pod sized -o jsonpath='{.status.qosClass}'

Lab 6.2: limitrange defaults

Domain: Workloads | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-02-limitrange-defaults)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace lr, create a LimitRange defaults so that containers without their own settings get a default CPU request of 100m, a default memory request of 64Mi, a default CPU limit of 250m and a default memory limit of 128Mi. Then create a Pod plain (image nginx:alpine) with no resource settings and show that it received the defaults.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n lr apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata: {name: defaults}
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Container
    defaultRequest: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}
    default: {cpu: 250m, memory: 128Mi}
Y
kubectl -n lr run plain --image=nginx:alpine
kubectl -n lr wait --for=condition=Ready pod/plain --timeout=120s
kubectl -n lr get pod plain -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].resources}'

Lab 6.3: resourcequota

Domain: Workloads | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-03-resourcequota)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace quota, create a ResourceQuota team-quota that allows at most 3 Pods, a total of 1 CPU in requests and 1Gi of memory in requests. Then create a Deployment app with 5 replicas of nginx:alpine whose containers request 100m CPU and 64Mi memory each. Because of the quota, at most 3 Pods can run; find the reason in the events or the ReplicaSet.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n quota create quota team-quota --hard=pods=3,requests.cpu=1,requests.memory=1Gi
kubectl -n quota create deployment app --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=5
kubectl -n quota set resources deployment app --requests=cpu=100m,memory=64Mi
sleep 10
kubectl -n quota get pods
kubectl -n quota describe rs | grep -i -E "exceeded|forbidden" | head -3
kubectl -n quota describe quota team-quota

Lab 6.4: nodeselector

Domain: Workloads | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-04-nodeselector)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Label the node cka-worker2 with disk=ssd. In the namespace sched, create a Pod fast (image nginx:alpine) that can only run on nodes with this label, and check that it runs on cka-worker2.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl label node cka-worker2 disk=ssd
kubectl -n sched apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: fast}
spec:
  nodeSelector: {disk: ssd}
  containers:
  - {name: web, image: "nginx:alpine"}
Y
kubectl -n sched wait --for=condition=Ready pod/fast --timeout=120s
kubectl -n sched get pod fast -o wide

Lab 6.5: node affinity

Domain: Workloads | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-05-node-affinity)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The node cka-worker carries the label tier=gold. In the namespace aff, create a Deployment gold-app with 3 replicas of nginx:alpine that must be scheduled only on nodes whose label tier is gold. Use node affinity (requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution), not nodeSelector.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n aff apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: gold-app}
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: gold-app}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: gold-app}}
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:
            - matchExpressions:
              - {key: tier, operator: In, values: [gold]}
      containers:
      - {name: web, image: "nginx:alpine"}
Y
kubectl -n aff rollout status deployment gold-app --timeout=120s
kubectl -n aff get pods -o wide

Lab 6.6: taint toleration

Domain: Workloads | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-06-taint-toleration)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Taint the node cka-worker2 with dedicated=db:NoSchedule. In the namespace taint, create a Pod db (image nginx:alpine) that tolerates this taint and is placed on cka-worker2 using nodeSelector on the label kubernetes.io/hostname.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl taint node cka-worker2 dedicated=db:NoSchedule
kubectl -n taint apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: db}
spec:
  nodeSelector: {kubernetes.io/hostname: cka-worker2}
  tolerations:
  - {key: dedicated, operator: Equal, value: db, effect: NoSchedule}
  containers:
  - {name: web, image: "nginx:alpine"}
Y
kubectl -n taint wait --for=condition=Ready pod/db --timeout=120s

Lab 6.7: pod anti affinity

Domain: Workloads | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-07-pod-anti-affinity)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace spread, create a Deployment ha-web with 2 replicas of nginx:alpine. Make the scheduler guarantee that the two Pods never run on the same node, using required Pod anti-affinity on the node hostname (kubernetes.io/hostname) for Pods with the label app=ha-web.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n spread apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: ha-web}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: ha-web}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: ha-web}}
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - labelSelector:
              matchLabels: {app: ha-web}
            topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
      containers:
      - {name: web, image: "nginx:alpine"}
Y
kubectl -n spread rollout status deployment ha-web --timeout=120s
kubectl -n spread get pods -o wide

Lab 6.8: fix pending pod

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-08-fix-pending-pod)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace pend, the Pod big stays Pending. Find the reason with kubectl describe and fix it so the Pod runs. Keep the Pod name big and the image nginx:alpine; a CPU request above 500m is not acceptable. (A Pod's resources cannot be edited in place; recreate it.)

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n pend describe pod big | grep -i -A2 "FailedScheduling"
kubectl -n pend delete pod big --force --grace-period 0
kubectl -n pend apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: big}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: web
    image: nginx:alpine
    resources:
      requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}
Y
kubectl -n pend wait --for=condition=Ready pod/big --timeout=120s

Lab 6.9: hpa

Domain: Workloads | Points: 8 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-09-hpa)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace auto, the Deployment scaler (nginx:alpine, 2 replicas) exists without resource requests. Configure autoscaling for it: give the container a CPU request of 100m, and create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler named scaler that keeps between 2 and 6 replicas and targets 60% average CPU utilization. The HPA must report its current CPU metric (not <unknown>).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n auto set resources deployment scaler --requests=cpu=100m
kubectl -n auto rollout status deployment scaler --timeout=120s
kubectl -n auto autoscale deployment scaler --min=2 --max=6 --cpu=60%
for i in $(seq 1 30); do [ -n "$(kubectl -n auto get hpa scaler -o jsonpath='{.status.currentMetrics[0].resource.current.averageUtilization}' 2>/dev/null)" ] && break; sleep 5; done
kubectl -n auto get hpa scaler

Lab 6.10: topology spread

Domain: Workloads | Points: 8 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-10-topology-spread)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace tsc, create a Deployment even with 4 replicas of nginx:alpine (label app=even) that must be spread evenly across the nodes: use a topology spread constraint on the node hostname (kubernetes.io/hostname) with maxSkew: 1, and do not schedule a Pod if the constraint cannot be met (DoNotSchedule). The control plane node is tainted and cannot run these Pods, so it must not count as an empty domain: set nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor. Both worker nodes must end up with 2 Pods each.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n tsc apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: even}
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: even}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: even}}
    spec:
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
        whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
        nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor
        labelSelector: {matchLabels: {app: even}}
      containers:
      - {name: web, image: "nginx:alpine"}
Y
kubectl -n tsc rollout status deployment even --timeout=120s
kubectl -n tsc get pods -o wide

<!-- /LABS -->

8Recall questions

R1A Pod is Pending. Where is the reason?

Show the answer

The FailedScheduling event in kubectl describe pod.

R2What happens to a container that exceeds its memory limit? Its CPU limit?

Show the answer

Memory: OOM-killed. CPU: throttled.

R3Which QoS class has requests equal to limits for every container?

Show the answer

Guaranteed.

R4What is the difference between a LimitRange and a ResourceQuota?

Show the answer

LimitRange sets defaults and bounds per container or Pod; ResourceQuota caps the namespace total.

R5A Deployment in a namespace with a Pod-count quota stops at 3 Pods. Where do you see why?

Show the answer

In the events of the ReplicaSet (describe rs) or kubectl get events.

R6Does a toleration make a Pod run on the tainted node?

Show the answer

No; it only allows it. Add a nodeSelector or affinity to attract it.

R7Which taint effect evicts running Pods?

Show the answer

NoExecute.

R8What two things does an HPA on CPU need?

Show the answer

The Metrics Server and a CPU request on the Pods.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Pending Pod describe pod, read FailedScheduling
Resources requests schedule, limits cap; memory over limit = OOMKilled
QoS Guaranteed, Burstable, BestEffort
Admission LimitRange (defaults/bounds), ResourceQuota (namespace total)
Placement nodeSelector, node affinity, pod (anti-)affinity, topology spread
Taint k taint node n key=value:effect; remove with key-
Toleration allows, does not attract
HPA k autoscale ... --min --max --cpu=50%; needs Metrics Server and CPU requests
